steps.title: Why the pawns cannot just run
steps.source: In the above position White can't win by 1 P - B 5. Black's best answer would be P - Kt 3 draws. […] He cannot win by 1 P - Kt 5, because P - Kt 3 draws. (This, because of the principle of the "opposition" which governs this ending.)

narration.say: Two connected pawns against one. But neither pawn can simply run.
After f5 or g5, Black answers g6 and draws.
The reason is the opposition, which Capablanca explains later. For now: the king leads.
Your move. Remember the lesson of the previous example.

exercise.prompt: White to move. How does White start?

feedback.f5: Black answers g6, and the game is drawn.
feedback.g5: Black answers g6, and the game is drawn.
feedback.*: Bring the king forward, next to the pawns.

exercise.hint: The king steps diagonally forward, towards the pawns.
exercise.success: 1. Ke4. Black stays in front with Ke6.

steps.title: The pawns advance, protected
steps.source: 2 P - B 5 ch, K - B 3; 3 K - B 4, P - Kt 3. (If this Pawn is kept back we arrive at the ending shown in Example 7.)

narration.say: Pawn to f5, check. Black to f6.
King to f4. Black plays g6. If he kept the pawn back, we would be in the previous example.
Pawn to g5, check. Black to f7.
Pawn to f6. Black to e6.
King to e4, and Black returns to f7.
King to e5. Black to f8.

steps.title: Your turn: give one to take one
steps.source: White cannot force his Bishop's Pawn into Q (find out why), but by giving his Pawn up he can win the other Pawn and the game.

narration.say: White cannot force the f-pawn to queen. But by giving it up, he can win the other pawn, and the game.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Give up the f-pawn in the right way.

feedback.*: Push the f-pawn: Black must spend time taking it.

exercise.hint: The f-pawn goes forward one more square.

narration.say: King to d6. Black to f8.
King to e6. Black to g7.
King to e7. Black to g8.
King to f6. Black to h7.
King to f7. Black to h8.
And the king takes the pawn on g6. Black to g8.

steps.title: Your turn: the only way
steps.source: There is still some resistance in Black's position. In fact, the only way to win is the one given here. 15 K - R 6 (if K - B 6, K - R 2; and in order to win White must get back to the actual position, as against 16 P - Kt 6 ch, K - R 1 draws).

narration.say: There is still some resistance. Only one move wins cleanly here.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the only clean win.

feedback.Kf6: After Kf6, Black plays Kh7, and g6 check, Kh8 would be a draw. White would have to come back.
feedback.Kf5: Too far away. Stay close to the black king.
feedback.*: Put your king where the pawn can advance with the king protecting it, and the black king cannot get in front.

exercise.hint: The king goes to the edge, next to the pawn.

narration.say: Pawn to g6. Black to g8.
Pawn to g7. Black to f7.
King to h7, and the pawn queens.

steps.title: What we learned
steps.source: This ending, apparently so simple, should show the student the enormous difficulties to be surmounted, even when there are hardly any pieces left.

narration.say: Even with very few pieces, the ending can be hard.
Sometimes you give up one pawn to win the other.
And these elementary things are the basis of true mastership in chess.
